x: Nagoya is Japan's automobile centre; Osaka is a textile centre and Yokohama a shipbuilding centre.

x: Baku is Azerbaijan's oil city; Glasgow, Yokohama and Hamburg are shipbuilding centres.

s: Dresden in Germany is known for which industry?
x: Dresden makes optical goods; Amsterdam and Antwerp cut diamonds and Abadan refines oil.

s: Which city is known as the Detroit of India?
x: Chennai is the Detroit of India; Osaka is the Manchester of the East and Chotanagpur the Ruhr of India.

s: St. Petersburg is a well-known centre of which industry?
x: St. Petersburg, like Glasgow, Yokohama and Hamburg, is a shipbuilding centre.

s: Which pair of cities is known for diamond cutting?
x: Amsterdam and Antwerp are the diamond-cutting centres.

x: Abadan in Iran is a major oil-refining centre; Baku is the oil centre of Azerbaijan.

x: Osaka in Kansai, Honshu, is the Manchester of the East and also the 'Nation's Kitchen'.

s: Why are most iron and steel plants of Japan located on the coast?
o: They use iron ore and coal imported in big ships
They are close to inland iron-ore mines
They depend on hydropower from rivers
x: Japan's steel industry is market-based: it imports ore and coal in big ships, so plants stand at ports on the coast.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Donbas is an iron and steel region of Ukraine, with Donetsk as its key centre.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
x: Metz and Nancy are centres of the Lorraine region in France. Essen, Duisburg and Dortmund are centres of the Ruhr region.

s: Magnitogorsk and Chelyabinsk are iron and steel centres of which region?
x: Magnitogorsk and Chelyabinsk are in the Ural region of Russia.

s: Hamilton, known as the 'Steel City', is located in which country?
x: Hamilton, at the western end of Lake Ontario, is the Steel City of Canada.

s: What does the 'Rust Belt' or 'Rust Bowl' refer to?
o: new software corridor of southern India
old manufacturing belt of the north-eastern USA and Great Lakes
x: Rust Belt or Rust Bowl denotes the old manufacturing belt of the north-eastern United States and the Great Lakes region.

s: Where is the Midlands industrial region located?
x: The Midlands is an industrial region of England, not of the United States.

s: Which regions does the Industrial Triangle of Northern Italy cover?
x: The Industrial Triangle covers Lombardy, Piedmont and Liguria; it grew on skilled labour, the market and hydropower.

s: Which ports support the development of the Pearl River Delta?
x: The ports of Hong Kong and Shenzhen, an export economy and cheap labour support the Pearl River Delta.

s: In which country is Gauteng, a mining-based steel and automotive region?
x: Gauteng is South Africa's mining and steel centre; São Paulo is in Brazil, Ontario–St. Lawrence in Canada and Silesia in Poland.

s: Kinki, comprising Osaka, Kobe and Kyoto, is best described as a:
o: dense industrial belt with textiles and heavy industry
x: Kinki is a dense industrial belt of Japan associated with textiles and heavy industry.

s: Which of the following industrial region – location pairs is wrongly matched?
x: The Donbas (Donetsk Basin) is in Ukraine with Donetsk as its centre; Kemerovo belongs to the Kuzbass.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ruhr region?
o: It lies in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.
It drew iron ore from Lorraine.
It drew iron ore from within the Ruhr itself.
Its industries include iron and steel, automobiles and chemicals.
x: The Ruhr's iron ore came from Lorraine, not from the Ruhr itself.

s: Which industrial region is known for iron and steel, heavy machinery and defence industries?
x: The Urals have iron and steel, heavy machinery and defence; Northern Italy has textiles and fashion, the Pearl River Delta electronics and toys, Ontario–St. Lawrence steel, cars and paper.

s: The Ruhr, the Yangtze River Delta, Moscow–Tula and São Paulo all list which industry among their key industries?
x: All four regions list chemicals among their key industries.

s: Which industrial region – basis of growth pair is correctly matched?
o: Midlands – early Industrial Revolution, coal and iron ore
x: The Midlands grew with the early Industrial Revolution, coal, iron ore and the canal and rail network.

s: In which country is the Ural industrial region, which grew on minerals such as iron and copper?
x: The Ural Region is in Russia and developed on mineral resources such as iron and copper.

s: Essen, Dortmund and Duisburg are centres of which industrial region?
x: Essen, Dortmund and Duisburg are Ruhr centres; Kuzbass has Kemerovo and Keihin is Tokyo–Yokohama.

s: On which cities is the Keihin industrial region of Japan centred?
x: Keihin is Tokyo–Yokohama, which grew on port facilities, skilled labour, technology and market.

s: Which is the oldest industrial region of the USA, which grew from textiles to a diversified base?
x: New England is the oldest US industrial region; Silicon Valley is the high-tech and aerospace hub.

s: Which industrial region is known for electronics and light manufacturing rather than heavy machinery?
x: The Pearl River Delta is known for electronics and light manufacturing; Manchuria has heavy industry, Moscow–Tula engineering and metallurgy, and Lorraine iron and steel.

s: From where does the Great Lakes Manufacturing Belt get its iron ore?
x: The belt grew on Mesabi Range iron ore, Appalachian coal, lake transport and skilled labour.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Lancashire, including Manchester, is a major cotton-textile region of the United Kingdom.

s: For which industry is the Flanders industrial region of Belgium known?
x: Flanders in Belgium is known for woollen and linen textiles.

s: Kemerovo is a centre of which industrial region?
x: Kemerovo lies in the Kuzbass (Kuznetsk Basin) of Siberia, not in the Donbas.

s: From where did the Ruhr iron and steel industry obtain its iron ore?
x: The Ruhr's iron ore came from Lorraine, not from the Ruhr itself.

s: The Ural industrial region is rich in which of the following minerals?
x: The Ural is the richest mineral region, with iron, copper, platinum, gold and precious stones.

s: For which industry is the Great Kanawha Valley region of the USA known?
x: The Great Kanawha Valley in West Virginia is a chemical industry region.

s: In which part of the United Kingdom is the Tweed valley, known for woollen tweed cloth?
x: The Tweed valley lies in Scotland, on the Scotland-England border, and gives its name to tweed cloth.

s: In which country is the Silesia coal and steel region?
x: Silesia is a coal and steel region of Poland.

s: In which country is the São Paulo industrial region, known for automobiles and chemicals?
x: São Paulo in Brazil is a major region of automobiles and chemicals.

s: The Industrial Triangle of Northern Italy grew mainly on which source of power?
x: Lombardy, Piedmont and Liguria grew on skilled labour, market and hydropower from the Alps.

s: In which province of China is the Pearl River Delta industrial region, known for electronics and toys?
x: The Pearl River Delta is in Guangdong, served by Hong Kong and Shenzhen.

s: Which country, along with India, makes up the top two steel-producing countries?
x: Steel leadership has shifted to China and India, the top two producers, while the Ruhr, Lorraine and the US Rust Belt declined.

s: What is India's steel capacity target for 2030?
x: India's capacity is about 220 MT and the 2030 target is 300 MT; India is second with 168.4 MT of crude steel.

s: Which is the oldest public-sector steel plant in South India?
x: VISL Bhadravati is the oldest public-sector steel plant in the south.

s: The term 'Asian Tigers' in the context of newly industrialising economies refers to which one of the following groups?
o: South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Hong Kong
Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam and the Philippines
South Korea, China, Singapore and Malaysia

x: China is first in steel with over 50 percent of world output; India is second.

s: Which country led the world in shipbuilding new orders in 2025?
x: China was first (about 60-66 percent), South Korea second and Japan third.

x: The revised index (base 2022-23) added iron ore, making nine core industries.

s: Which country was the leading producer of cotton textiles in 2025?
x: China led world cotton textile production in 2025.

s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of footloose industries?
o: They are necessarily highly polluting heavy industries.
They are generally light, high-value and have low transport costs.
They can operate only in mining regions.
They must be located beside bulky raw materials.
x: Footloose industries are generally light, high-value, low in transport cost and low in pollution, and are not tied to a raw material or fixed location, e.g. diamond cutting, electronics, software and watch-making. They are not heavy polluting, mining-bound or raw-material-bound industries.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about agglomeration economies?
o: They explain why footloose industries such as diamond cutting must locate next to raw materials
They arise through shared infrastructure, specialised suppliers and a skilled labour pool
They are cost savings firms obtain when they cluster
Mumbai-Pune, Chennai-Bengaluru and Delhi-NCR are examples of such clusters
x: Footloose industries like diamond cutting are by definition not tied to raw-material sites.

s: In which year was the term 'Umland' first used?
x: Umland, the area around a town linked to it economically and culturally, was first used in 1883.

s: What is the area surrounding a town or city that is economically linked to it called?
x: The umland is the area economically tied to a town.

s: Which of the following is called a 'sunrise industry'?
x: Information technology and electronics are sunrise industries.

s: About how many tonnes of raw materials are needed to produce one tonne of steel?
x: About four tonnes of iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite make one tonne of steel, so plants locate near coalfields or ore fields.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the main inputs needed to make steel?
x: About 4 tonnes of iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite make 1 tonne of steel; bauxite is not among them.

s: According to Weber’s least-cost theory, an industrial firm seeks a location where the combined cost of which factors is least?
o: Raw materials, climate and exports only
x: Alfred Weber’s 1909 least-cost theory considers the combined transport, labour and agglomeration costs.

s: In Weber's terms, what kind of material is raw cotton, so that cotton textile mills are not bound to raw-cotton sites?
x: Raw cotton is non-weight-losing, so cotton textile mills are not necessarily tied to raw-cotton sites.

s: What do the three vertices of Weber's locational triangle represent?
o: one raw-material source and two ports only
two markets and one labour centre
two raw-material sources and one market
x: The locational triangle consists of two raw-material sources and one market. The least-transport-cost point lies inside the triangle.

s: In Weber's least-cost theory, isodapanes are lines joining places of equal:
x: Isodapanes join points of equal extra transport cost.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its material category?
x: Water and air are ubiquitous materials available everywhere. Cotton is treated as a pure localised material, while iron ore is a gross or weight-losing material.

s: In Weber's theory, what is the Material Index the ratio of?
o: weight of finished product to weight of localised raw materials
weight of localised raw materials to weight of finished product
x: Material Index = weight of localised raw materials / weight of the finished product.

s: According to Weber, where does an industry with a Material Index greater than 1 locate?
x: MI > 1 means a weight-losing process, which pulls the industry to the raw material; MI < 1 pulls it to the market.

s: In which year did Alfred Weber put forward his least-cost theory of industrial location?
x: Weber's least-cost theory dates from 1909.

s: Who introduced the Location Quotient?
x: P. Sargant Florence introduced the Location Quotient; Hoover dealt with transport-cost structure, Isard the substitution principle and Losch the maximum-profit market-area approach.

s: In whose approach are ports and break-of-bulk points favoured industrial locations?
x: Hoover's emphasis on transport-cost structure and terminal costs favours ports and break-of-bulk points.

s: With whom is the substitution principle of industrial location associated?
x: Walter Isard gave the substitution principle, a trade-off between transport and other costs.

s: Who gave the maximum-profit or market-area approach to industrial location?
x: August Losch gave the maximum-profit (market-area) approach; Weber gave least cost.

x: Koyali is an oil-refinery centre.

s: Singrauli is called an 'energy enclave' because of its:
x: Singrauli is a coal and thermal power centre, the energy enclave.

s: Which of the following centre – industry pairs is wrongly matched?
x: Modinagar is a rubber centre; Aonla and Panki are the fertiliser centres.

s: Which town of Tamil Nadu, called 'Little Japan' by Nehru, is known for fireworks and matches?
x: Sivakasi in Virudhunagar district is famous for fireworks, matches and printing; Nehru called it Little Japan.

s: For which industry is Bhiwandi in Maharashtra known?
x: Bhiwandi near Mumbai is a powerloom centre.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Sugar is raw-material-based because cane is weight-losing and perishable. Bakery is market-based (B wrong), iron and steel is raw-material-based, about 4 t of input per tonne (C wrong), and cement is raw-material-based on limestone, not footloose (D wrong).

x: Market-based industries such as bakeries and soft-drink production locate near consumers because their products are weight-gaining or fragile.

s: The steel belt is concentrated on the Chota Nagpur Plateau mainly because the principal raw materials of steel are:
x: Steel's raw materials are weight-losing, so they are processed most cheaply near their source on the Chota Nagpur Plateau.

s: The term ‘footloose industries’ refers to industries which generally
o: use light inputs and have negligible transport costs
depend mainly on coalfields and iron-ore deposits
require very large quantities of bulky raw material at the production site
x: Footloose industries use light inputs, incur negligible transport costs and are not tightly tied to a particular raw-material source.

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of examples of footloose industries?
o: Diamond polishing, electronics assembly and software
Iron and steel, software and sugar
Iron and steel, sugar and cement
x: Diamond polishing, electronics assembly and software are identified as footloose industries. Iron and steel, sugar and cement are associated with raw-material orientation, while aluminium is power-oriented.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alfred Weber's least-cost theory?
o: A Material Index above 1 pulls the industry towards the market
A plant first locates where total transport cost is lowest, then adjusts for labour and agglomeration
A Material Index below 1, or ubiquitous inputs such as water, favours the market
x: MI above 1 (weight-losing inputs, e.g. iron and steel, sugar) pulls the plant to the raw material, not the market.

s: In Weber's least-cost theory, where can an industry using a 'pure' raw material such as cotton, which loses no weight in processing, be located?
o: Anywhere between the source and the market
x: A pure raw material has no weight loss, so transport cost is the same whether raw material or product is moved; the plant is free to locate anywhere between source and market. Weight-losing inputs (MI > 1) pull it to the source (A); weight-gaining or ubiquitous inputs (MI < 1) pull it to the market (B); a port location (D) is not implied by the theory.

s: Which one of the following pairs of cities is associated with clustering of footloose industries?
x: Bengaluru and Hyderabad are among the identified clusters of footloose industries; Pune and Noida are also included in this group.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about factors of industrial location?
o: Proximity to raw material can reduce transport cost
Skilled and inexpensive labour may influence location
Tax concessions and subsidies can affect location
Access to water is irrelevant to industrial location
x: Water is an important location factor for several industries, so it is not irrelevant.

s: Towards which factor is the aluminium industry primarily oriented?
x: Aluminium is power-oriented, needing 14,000-15,000 kWh per tonne.

s: Which one of the following industrial regions is associated with Jamshedpur, Ranchi, Dhanbad and Bokaro?
x: Jamshedpur, Ranchi, Dhanbad and Bokaro are major centres of the Chotanagpur industrial region, known as the ‘Ruhr of India’.

s: The growth of the Chotanagpur industrial region is closely linked to the availability of:
x: Chotanagpur's growth is closely linked to the discovery and availability of coal, along with other minerals.

s: Which Indian city, hosting Hyundai, Renault-Nissan, Ashok Leyland and Daimler, is called the 'Detroit of India'?
x: Chennai is the 'Detroit of India' because of its large cluster of automobile makers. Pune (A), Gurugram-Manesar (C) and Sanand (D) are also automobile hubs but do not carry this nickname.

s: Which of the following industrial region – principal industries pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu – IT, aerospace, biotechnology and electronics
Visakhapatnam-Guntur – Steel, shipbuilding, petroleum and fertilisers
Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut – Automobiles, electronics and light industry
x: Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram is known for cashew, coir and rubber; steel, shipbuilding and petroleum belong to Visakhapatnam-Guntur.

s: Which industrial region of India is described as an 'industrial workshop' for its textile, pharmaceutical and petrochemical industries?
x: Coastal Gujarat is called an industrial workshop because of its textile, pharmaceutical and petrochemical industries.

s: Which of the following automobile hubs is located in Andhra Pradesh and is associated with Isuzu and Kobelco?
x: Sri City in Andhra Pradesh is identified as an automobile hub associated with Isuzu and Kobelco.

s: Which one of the following is a minor industrial belt of Madhya Pradesh?
x: Indore-Dewas-Pithampur is a minor industrial belt of Madhya Pradesh. Mandideep near Bhopal is another such belt in the state.

s: Which regions of India are described as its industrial powerhouses?
x: Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka (South and West) are powerhouses, while the East, North-East and parts of the North lag.

s: The Hugli industrial region is chiefly known for which industry?
x: Hugli is the jute region; Rishra had the first jute mill in 1855.

s: For which industries is the Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram industrial region known?
x: Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram is known for cashew, coir and rubber.

s: Pimpri and Nashik belong to which industrial region?
x: Mumbai-Pune includes Mumbai, Thane, Trombay, Pune, Pimpri, Nashik and Solapur.

s: Which one of the following is a minor industrial belt of India?
x: Durg-Raipur is a minor belt; Hugli, Mumbai-Pune and Chotanagpur are major industrial regions.

s: Which industrial region of India is called the 'Ruhr of India'?
x: The Chotanagpur region, with its coal and iron ore, is called the Ruhr of India.

s: Where was the first jute mill of the Hugli industrial region set up in 1855?
x: The first jute mill came up at Rishra, near Kolkata, in 1855.

s: Manufacturing currently contributes about what share of India's GDP?
x: Manufacturing contributes about 16–17% of GDP; the target is 25% by 2047.

s: Vallarpadam, cited as an SEZ example, is located in which State?
x: Vallarpadam is an SEZ example from Kerala; Nanguneri is the one from Tamil Nadu.

s: As on 31 March 2025, how many SEZs were notified and operational in India respectively?
x: As on 31 March 2025, India had 368 notified SEZs, of which 276 were operational.

s: Under which of the following were National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) introduced?
x: NIMZs come under the National Manufacturing Policy 2011, which targeted manufacturing at 25% of GDP and 100 million jobs.

s: The BHAVYA scheme provides for how many plug-and-play industrial parks?
x: BHAVYA provides for 100 parks with ₹33,660 crore over FY 2026–27 to 2031–32, chosen in challenge mode and run by NICDC.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs)?
o: They follow exactly the same governance and fiscal rules as SEZs
They differ from SEZs in exit rules
x: NIMZs differ from SEZs in governance, exit and fiscal rules, so saying they follow exactly the same rules is wrong.

s: Which is the nodal agency managing about 571 industrial parks in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) is the nodal agency and manages 571 industrial parks. NICDC (A) and NICDIT (D) are national corridor bodies; APFDC (C) is the AP Forest Development Corporation.

s: What share of GDP for manufacturing did the National Manufacturing Policy 2011, which introduced NIMZs, target?
x: The policy targeted manufacturing at 25 percent of GDP and 100 million jobs; manufacturing is now about 16-17 percent.

s: In which State is the Nanguneri SEZ located?
x: Nanguneri SEZ is in Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu; Vallarpadam is in Kerala.

s: How many jobs did the National Manufacturing Policy 2011 aim to create?
x: The 2011 policy, which brought NIMZs, aimed at 25% manufacturing share of GDP and 100 million jobs.

s: Which body runs the BHAVYA scheme of 100 plug-and-play industrial parks?
x: BHAVYA (₹33,660 crore, 2026-27 to 2031-32) is run by NICDC in challenge mode.

s: Which State has the largest number of operational Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India?
x: As per the Commerce Ministry (March 2025), Tamil Nadu has 58 notified and 49 operational SEZs, the most in India.

s: On which date did the SEZ Act, 2005 come into force?
x: The SEZ Act, 2005 came into force on 10 February 2006.

s: Which city is NOT a node of the Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor?
x: The five nodes are Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem and Tiruchirappalli; Madurai is not one.

s: India’s first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along which stretch?
x: India’s first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along the Chennai-Bengaluru stretch.

s: The Delhi–Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) is being developed with which partner country?
x: DMIC, covering Delhi, UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat and Maharashtra, has Japan as its partner.

s: Which agency backs the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)?
x: VCIC is backed by the ADB; Japan partners the DMIC and the UK the BMEC.

s: Between which places does the East Coast Economic Corridor extend?
x: The East Coast Economic Corridor extends from Kolkata to Kanyakumari.

s: Which country is the partner for the Bengaluru–Mumbai Economic Corridor (BMEC)?
x: The UK is the BMEC partner; CBIC is with Japan through JICA and VCIC with the ADB.

s: The Budget 2026-27 proposed an integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor with a node at which place?
x: The integrated East Coast Industrial Corridor proposed in Budget 2026-27 includes a node at Durgapur under the Purvodaya initiative.

s: The Krishnapatnam node belongs to which industrial corridor?

x: NICDC (ex-DMICDC) was set up in January 2008; August 2024 is when 12 new industrial smart cities were approved.

s: Which are the Andhra Pradesh nodes of the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)?

x: AKIC uses the Eastern DFC; DMIC is built along the Western DFC.

s: How many national industrial corridors are there under NICDP?
x: There are 11 corridors under NICDP; 12 new industrial smart cities were approved in August 2024.

s: Which is the Andhra Pradesh node of the Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (HBIC)?
x: HBIC's AP node is Orvakal in Kurnool; Krishnapatnam is the CBIC node.

s: Which of the following States is NOT covered by the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)?
x: DMIC runs through Delhi, UP, Haryana, Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat and Maharashtra; Punjab is not on it.

too large and free of regulatory barriers

Public-sector plants at Salem, Visakhapatnam and Vijayanagar were placed right next to their raw materials

s: Which was India's first public-sector integrated steel plant?
x: Rourkela (Odisha), built with German help, was the first public-sector integrated plant.

s: In which year was the Prime Minister's Trophy for the best integrated steel plant instituted?
x: The trophy was instituted in 1992-93; SAIL Bhilai holds the record with 11 wins.

s: Which one of the following is NOT one of SAIL's three special steel plants?
x: SAIL's special steel plants are Salem, Durgapur and Bhadravati; Bhilai is one of its five integrated plants.

s: Which is the oldest public-sector steel plant in South India?

s: Which steel plant holds the record for the most wins of the Prime Minister's Trophy for the best integrated steel plant?
x: SAIL Bhilai holds the record with 11 wins of the Prime Minister's Trophy, instituted in 1992-93.

s: In which year was TISCO at Jamshedpur set up?

s: With the help of which country was the Durgapur steel plant set up?
x: Durgapur was built with British help; Bhilai and Bokaro with the USSR and Rourkela with Germany.

s: Which of the following steel plants was set up before independence?
x: VISL Bhadravati dates from 1923; Bhilai, Rourkela and Bokaro were built after independence.

s: At the confluence of which rivers does the Bokaro steel plant lie?
x: Bokaro stands at the confluence of the Damodar and Bokaro rivers; TISCO is at the Subarnarekha-Kharkai confluence.

s: In which State is the Vijayanagar steel plant located?

x: Bhilai is primarily an iron and steel centre; Jamnagar, Vadodara and Haldia are the petrochemical centres.

x: Bokaro Steel Plant was established with USSR collaboration. Bhilai, Rourkela and Durgapur were respectively associated with the USSR, West Germany and the UK.

x: Salem, Visakhapatnam and Vijayanagar are examples of plants located away from the principal raw-material areas for balanced regional development.

s: Coastal steel plants such as Visakhapatnam, Hazira and Dolvi mainly import coking coal from which country?
x: Coastal plants use imported coking coal, mainly from Australia.

x: Vedanta's Jharsuguda (Odisha) is the largest smelter; Angul is NALCO's smelter.

x: NALCO's plants are at Damanjodi and Angul; Korba belongs to BALCO and Renukoot to HINDALCO.

x: INDAL is linked with Muri, Alupuram and Belagavi, not Jharsuguda. Jharsuguda has India's largest aluminium smelter, run by Vedanta. BALCO–Korba, NALCO–Damanjodi and HINDALCO–Renukoot are correct.

s: What was India's crude steel production in 2025-26?

s: What is India's rank in world crude steel production?

x: The draft brings iron and steel under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, with cuts for 255 plants from FY 2026-27.

x: Odisha leads sponge iron, followed by Chhattisgarh, then West Bengal and Jharkhand.

s: Which organisation operates the copper facilities at Khetri and Ghatsila–Mosabani?
x: Khetri in Rajasthan and Ghatsila–Mosabani in Jharkhand are copper centres operated by Hindustan Copper Limited.

o: the largest aluminium smelter in India
the first public integrated steel plant

x: Hindustan Zinc runs a zinc smelter at Visakhapatnam and a lead-zinc unit at Zawar, Rajasthan.

s: Which of the following was among the alternative sites considered before Visakhapatnam was selected for the steel plant?

x: The foundation stone was laid on 20 January 1971; the first blast furnace, Godavari, had its foundation in 1982.

s: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL) is India's first:

s: What is the main iron-ore source of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant?
x: Vizag steel's main ore source is Bailadila (Chhattisgarh), not Bellary.

x: Visakhapatnam (RINL) is the first shore-based plant; Hazira and Dolvi are later coastal plants.

x: Steelmaking is weight-losing (about four tonnes of inputs per tonne of steel), and Chota Nagpur provides iron ore, coking coal, limestone and dolomite.

s: Who established the first successful cotton mill of India in Mumbai in 1854?
x: C. N. Davar set up the first successful mill at Mumbai in 1854; the 1818 Fort Gloster mill had failed.

o: Jute, softwood and riverine retting water
Petroleum, imported wool and sea-borne coal
Hydel power, cheap labour and local cotton
x: Coimbatore's spinning concentration is supported by hydel power, cheap labour and local cotton.

x: Kota is a synthetic silk centre; Ludhiana is hosiery, Indore cotton textiles and Sakkar Nagar sugar.

x: India's first sugar mill came up at Pratappur in Deoria district of Uttar Pradesh in 1903.

s: The sugar industry is India's second-largest agro-based industry after which industry?
x: The sugar industry is India's second-largest agro-based industry, after cotton textiles.

o: is perishable and yields only about 9–12% sugar
is a pure raw material that loses no weight
x: Sugarcane is perishable and yields only about 9–12% sugar, so long-distance transport is uneconomic.

s: Which of the following pairs of sugar-producing areas and states is correctly matched?
x: Meerut, Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar form the western Uttar Pradesh sugar belt. Gorakhpur, Deoria and Basti are in eastern Uttar Pradesh, while the Godavari and Chittoor belts are in Andhra Pradesh.

x: India is second after Brazil, with about 19 per cent of world output, and is the largest consumer.

s: Which State accounts for about 35 per cent of India's sugar production?
x: Uttar Pradesh has about 35 per cent, Maharashtra 22, Karnataka 10 and Tamil Nadu 8 per cent.

x: Maharashtra (~9.9 MT) led sugar output, ahead of Uttar Pradesh (~8.9 MT) and Karnataka (~4.7 MT). UP (A) has the largest share in the long-run pattern (35%) but came second this season; Karnataka (B) was third; Tamil Nadu (D) is smaller.

s: For what is molasses, a by-product of the sugar industry, mainly used?
x: Molasses goes to alcohol and ethanol; bagasse is boiler fuel and paper pulp, press mud is manure.

x: Grain now provides about three-fourths of ethanol production, though molasses remains an important sugar-industry feedstock.

x: The Rangarajan Committee recommended a 70:30 revenue-sharing formula and removal of the minimum-distance rule.

s: Who fixes the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane?

x: Bagasse is used as boiler fuel and paper pulp; molasses gives alcohol and press mud is manure.

x: Press mud is used as manure; bagasse is fuel and pulp, molasses goes to ethanol.

s: Shakkar Nagar, which grew around the Nizam Sugar Factory, is near which town?
x: Shakkar Nagar at Bodhan in Nizamabad district (now Telangana) grew around the Nizam Sugar Factory.

s: Who fixes the State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane?
x: The Centre fixes the FRP; States may fix a higher State Advised Price (SAP).

x: India is the second largest sugar producer after Brazil and the largest consumer.

s: Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka are leading centres of which industry?

s: Nangal, Bhatinda and Panipat belong to which regional group of fertiliser plants?
x: Nangal, Bhatinda and Panipat form the North-West group; Sindri and the steel towns form the Chota Nagpur group, and Neyveli, Tuticorin, Ennore, Alwaye and Kochi the Tamil Nadu–Kerala group.

o: Naphtha, natural gas, coal, rock phosphate, sulphur and gypsum
Bamboo, bagasse, poplar, eucalyptus and rags
Limestone, silica, alumina, gypsum and fly ash
Raw cotton, jute, wool and silk

s: Which combination is identified as the key raw material combination for urea production?
x: Urea is made from ammonia (via the Haber process) and carbon dioxide. Rock phosphate with sulphuric acid makes superphosphate.

s: From where does the sulphur used in phosphatic fertiliser production mainly come?
x: Sulphur for making sulphuric acid comes from oil refineries; natural gas (mainly methane) is the ammonia feedstock.

s: Which one of the following sets represents the Gujarat–Maharashtra region identified as the largest fertiliser-producing region?
x: Vadodara, Kalol, Kandla and Trombay constitute the Gujarat–Maharashtra region, described as the largest regional concentration in the table.

s: Which State is the largest producer of urea in India?
x: Uttar Pradesh leads urea production, while Gujarat leads overall fertiliser production; India is the second-largest fertiliser consumer.

o: India's first public-sector integrated steel plant
India's oldest shipyard established by Scindia
the largest aluminium complex developed with French help
the world's largest refining complex operated by Reliance

x: India's per capita cement consumption is about 290 kg, compared with a world average of about 540 kg.

x: Jaggayyapeta is in NTR district; Yerraguntla is in Kadapa.

s: Which State ranked second in cement production in 2026?
x: Rajasthan is the largest cement State, followed by Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which mineral of the Kadapa-Kurnool area makes Rayalaseema a cement hub?
x: Kadapa-Kurnool limestone supports cement at Yerraguntla, Nandyal and other centres.

s: Which of the following combinations represents the principal inputs of the cement industry?
o: Raw jute, cotton, wool and local cane
Naphtha, natural gas, sulphur and rock phosphate
x: The principal cement inputs listed are limestone, silica, alumina and gypsum; fly ash and slag are also used.

s:
Consider the following statements about the raw materials of the paper industry:
1. Bagasse and bamboo are used as inputs.
2. Rock phosphate is used as an input.
3. Eucalyptus is used as an input.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Paper uses bamboo, bagasse, poplar, eucalyptus, softwood and rags. Rock phosphate is a fertiliser input, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Jagiroad is located in which State?
x: Jagiroad is in Assam; Sirpur is in Telangana, Rajahmundry in AP and Ballarpur in Maharashtra.

s: The Sirpur (Kagaznagar) paper mill is in which State?
x: Sirpur is in Telangana; Rajahmundry is in AP and Ballarpur in Maharashtra.

s: Which of the following pairs of paper mill and State is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Rajahmundry is in Andhra Pradesh; the other pairs are correct.

s: For which product is Nepanagar in Madhya Pradesh known?
x: Nepanagar in MP is India's well-known newsprint mill.

s: Approximately what proportion of India's jute mill capacity is concentrated in the belt along the Hooghly River?
x: About 90% of jute mill capacity is concentrated along the Hooghly basin.

s: Which jute scheme promotes certified seed and microbial retting using 'SONA'?
x: JUTE-ICARE promotes certified seed and microbial retting with SONA. The National Jute Development Programme (A) and Jute Diversification Scheme (B) are separate schemes; the Jute Packaging Materials Act 1987 (D) mandates jute bags for foodgrains and sugar.

s: Of India's 97 jute mills (2026), how many are in West Bengal?
x: West Bengal has 71 of the 97 mills and AP 12; West Bengal gives over 80% of jute output.

s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh:
1. Jute mills at Chittivalasa and Nellimarla have existed since the 1920s.
2. Rajahmundry is associated with the paper industry.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Chittivalasa and Nellimarla have had jute mills since the 1920s, and Rajahmundry is AP's paper centre.

s: What does the Jute Packaging Materials Act, 1987 make compulsory to pack in jute bags?
x: The Act provides for 100% of foodgrains and 20% of sugar to be packed in jute bags.

s: Which port supports the concentration of jute mills in the Hooghly basin?
x: Raw jute, the Hooghly waterway, Kolkata port and cheap labour explain the Hooghly concentration of jute mills.

s: In which year was the National Jute Policy announced?
x: The National Jute Policy dates to 2005; 1987 is the Jute Packaging Materials Act.

s: Bhatpara in West Bengal is a centre of which industry?
x: Bhatpara is a jute centre; Titagarh is a paper centre.

s: Which State has the second-largest number of jute mills in India?
x: Of 97 jute mills, West Bengal has 71 and Andhra Pradesh 12 (2nd).

s: Which country is the largest exporter of jute?
x: Bangladesh is the largest jute exporter, with about 75% share.

s: Which of the following is a reason for the concentration of jute mills along the Hooghly?
x: The Hooghly belt has raw jute, soft water for retting, the river, Kolkata port and cheap labour.

s:

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Bhatpara is associated with the jute industry.
Lakheri is associated with the cement industry.
Bhatpara is associated with the paper industry.
Titagarh is associated with the paper industry.
x: Option C is incorrect: Bhatpara is a jute centre, not paper. Lakheri cement and Titagarh paper are right.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Centre)
a. Alang
b. Digboi
c. Titagarh
d. Satna
List-II (Industry)
I. Paper
II. Cement
III. Ship-breaking
IV. Oil refinery
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Alang is for ship-breaking, Digboi for oil refining, Titagarh for paper and Satna for cement.

s: Where was India's first iron and steel unit on modern lines (1830) set up?
x: Porto Novo, Tamil Nadu (1830) was the first unit on modern lines; the first integrated plant was TISCO, Jamshedpur (1907).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The first jute mill was set up at Rishra, near Kolkata, in 1855. The other years are wrong: the first woollen mill was at Kanpur in 1876 (not 1907), the paper mill at Serampore in 1812 (not 1904), and the aircraft unit at Bengaluru in 1940 (not 1912).

s:
Arrange the following industrial units in chronological order of establishment:
1. Aircraft factory, Bengaluru
2. Super-phosphate factory, Ranipet
3. Paper mill, Serampore
4. Integrated steel plant, Jamshedpur
x: Serampore paper mill 1812, Ranipet super-phosphate 1906, Jamshedpur TISCO 1907, Bengaluru aircraft factory 1940.

s: Where was the first fertiliser public sector undertaking of India established?
x: Sindri in Jharkhand was the first fertiliser PSU and was established during the First Plan.

s: Which was the first industry to develop in India?
x: Cottage industry was the first industry to develop in India, long before modern mills. The first cotton mill came only in 1818.

s: Where was India's first jute mill set up in 1855?
x: The first jute mill came up at Rishra near Kolkata in 1855; Serampore had the first paper mill (1812).

s: Where was India's first paper mill (1812) set up?
x: The first paper mill was at Serampore, West Bengal, in 1812.

s: Where was India's first woollen mill (1876) set up?
x: The first woollen mill came up at Kanpur in 1876 as an army depot unit.

s: Where was India's first super-phosphate factory set up in 1906?
x: The first super-phosphate factory was set up at Ranipet in Tamil Nadu in 1906; Sindri was the first fertiliser PSU.

s: Which company set up a steel plant in India in 1870?
x: The Bengal Iron Works Company set up a steel plant in 1870; TISCO came in 1907.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding railway production units?
x: Integral Coach Factory (ICF) is located at Perambur in Chennai. RCF is at Kapurthala, Diesel Locomotive Works is at Varanasi and the Wheel and Axle Plant is at Bengaluru.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works in West Bengal produces electric locomotives.

s: In which year was the Rail Coach Factory at Kapurthala established?
x: RCF Kapurthala dates from 1988; 1984 is the Rail Wheel Factory and 1955 the ICF, Perambur.

s: In collaboration with which country was the Integral Coach Factory at Perambur (Chennai) set up in 1955?
x: ICF Perambur was set up in 1955 with Swiss collaboration. The USSR (A) helped Bhilai and Bokaro steel, West Germany (B) Rourkela, and Japan (D) is the DMIC partner.

s: About 60% of India's railway wagons come from which State?
x: About 60% of wagons come from West Bengal, and most wagons are built in the private sector.

s: Where is the Rail Wheel Factory (wheels and axles) located?
x: RWF (1984) is at Yelahanka, Bengaluru; Kapurthala is RCF and Chittaranjan is CLW.

s: Where is the Banaras Locomotive Works (formerly Diesel Locomotive Works) located?
x: BLW, the former DLW, is at Manduadih, Varanasi, and now makes electric locomotives.

s: What does the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works in West Bengal manufacture?
x: CLW at Chittaranjan makes electric locomotives; coaches come from ICF, RCF and MCF, wheels from RWF.

s: Where is the Modern Coach Factory, the third rail coach factory of India, located?
x: The Modern Coach Factory at Rae Bareli (foundation 2007) is the third coach factory, after ICF Perambur and RCF Kapurthala.

s: What was the earlier name of the Patiala Locomotive Works (PLW)?
x: PLW Patiala was earlier the Diesel Loco Modernisation Works (DMW); DLW Varanasi is now BLW.

s: Where is Mazagon Dock located?
x: Mazagon Dock is at Mumbai; Cochin Shipyard is at Kochi and Hindustan Shipyard (1941) at Visakhapatnam.

s: Which set of industrial facilities is located at Visakhapatnam?
o: SAIL steel plant, Cochin Shipyard and IOC refinery
RINL steel plant, Hindustan Shipyard and HPCL refinery
TISCO steel plant, Hindustan Shipyard and IOC refinery
RINL steel plant, Garden Reach Shipbuilders and BPCL refinery
x: Visakhapatnam has the RINL steel plant, Hindustan Shipyard and the HPCL refinery.

s: Where is India's oldest shipyard, Hindustan Shipyard (1941)?
x: Hindustan Shipyard at Visakhapatnam (1941) is the oldest; Cochin Shipyard is the largest.

s: Where is the largest ship-breaking yard of India?
x: Alang in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat, is India's largest ship-breaking yard.

s: Which is the largest shipyard of India?
x: Cochin Shipyard at Kochi is the largest; Hindustan Shipyard at Visakhapatnam is the oldest.

s:
Consider the following statements about Indian shipyards:
1. Cochin Shipyard is the largest shipyard.
2. Hindustan Shipyard, Visakhapatnam is the oldest.
3. The Alang-Sosiya ship-breaking yard is in Maharashtra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Cochin is the largest and Hindustan Shipyard (1941) the oldest; Alang-Sosiya is in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Where is Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) based?
x: GRSE is at Kolkata, with its diesel engine plant at Ranchi.

s: Where did the modern car industry in India begin with Premier Automobiles?
x: The modern car industry in India began with Premier Automobiles at Kurla in Mumbai in 1947.

s: In the Visakhapatnam–Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC), the southern and northern portions are associated respectively with:
x: The southern part of VCIC is associated with automobiles, whereas the northern part is associated with pharmaceuticals.

s: Where was TELCO (Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company) established in 1945?
x: TELCO was established at Jamshedpur in 1945.

s: Which city is known as the "Detroit of India"?
x: Chennai, home to Hyundai, BMW, Renault-Nissan and Ashok Leyland, is the Detroit of India.

s: The Kia car plant in Andhra Pradesh is in which district?
x: Kia is in Sri Sathya Sai district (Anantapur region); Sri City hosts Isuzu and Foxconn.

s: In which State is the Sanand automobile hub of Tata Motors and MG Motor?
x: Sanand in Gujarat hosts Tata Motors and MG Motor; it also has Micron's ATMP unit.

s: FAME India was introduced in 2015. In which year was FAME-II introduced?
x: FAME India began in 2015 and FAME-II was introduced in 2019.

s: What minimum domestic value addition does the PLI-Auto scheme (2021) require?
x: The PLI-Auto scheme, approved in 2021 with ₹25,938 crore, requires a minimum of 50% domestic value addition.

s: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme was announced in 2020 for how many sectors?
x: PLI covered 14 sectors with an outlay of ₹1.97 lakh crore.

s: What is the total outlay of the PLI scheme announced in 2020?
x: The 2020 PLI covers 14 sectors with ₹1.97 lakh crore; ₹25,938 crore is PLI-Auto.

s: Where was Heavy Engineering Corporation (HEC), India's first heavy-machinery unit, set up in 1958?
x: HEC was established at Ranchi in 1958 and was the first unit producing heavy machinery.

s: With which products is BHEL's Bhopal unit particularly associated?
x: BHEL Bhopal produces heavy electricals and traction motors; BHEL builds electric locomotives at Jhansi.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)?
o: It originated as Hindustan Aircraft in Bengaluru in 1940
Its Nashik unit is associated with MiG airframes
Its Koraput unit is associated with MiG engines
x: Hindustan Aircraft began in 1940, but HAL was formed in 1964.

s: What was the all-time high value of India's defence production in FY 2024-25?
x: Defence production reached an all-time high of Rs 1,51,339 crore in FY 2024-25. Rs 1.97 lakh crore (C) is the outlay of the PLI scheme for 14 sectors, not defence output.

s: When private participation in defence production was opened in May 2001, what was the permitted FDI?
x: Private participation in defence production was opened in May 2001, with FDI then permitted up to 26%.

s: With which product is HAL's unit at Koraput associated?
x: Koraput makes MiG engines; Nashik makes MiG airframes and Kanpur transport aircraft.

s:
Consider the following statements about the reorganisation of the Ordnance Factory Board:
1. Its 41 units were replaced by 7 DPSUs.
2. BEL is one of the new DPSUs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 41-unit OFB became 7 DPSUs, including Yantra India and India Optel; BEL is not one of them.

s: With which product is BHEL's Jhansi unit associated?
x: BHEL Jhansi makes electric locomotives; HEC Ranchi is the heavy-machinery unit.

s: In which year was Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) formed?
x: Hindustan Aircraft dates to 1940, but HAL was formed in 1964.

s: Which public sector company is the largest machine-tool maker of India?
x: HMT, with units at Bengaluru, Pinjore, Kalamassery, Hyderabad and others, is the largest machine-tool maker.

s: In which city is BHEL's Ramachandrapuram unit located?
x: BHEL's Ramachandrapuram unit is in Hyderabad; other units are at Bhopal, Haridwar, Jhansi, Tiruchirappalli and Ranipet.

s: In which city is Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), a defence electronics maker, located?
x: BEL at Bengaluru makes defence electronics.

s: With which product is HAL's Kanpur unit associated?
x: HAL Kanpur makes transport aircraft; Koraput makes MiG engines and Nashik MiG airframes.

s: Why is the IT industry described as 'footloose'?
o: It is independent of raw materials and is attracted by engineering talent and a technology ecosystem.
It can operate only near coalfields and ports.
It depends exclusively on bulky local raw materials.
It requires heavy mineral inputs at the production site.
x: The IT industry is footloose because it is largely independent of raw materials and is located mainly according to engineering talent and the technology ecosystem.

s: In which year were the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) set up?
x: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) were set up in 1991. Major IT clusters are Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai and Noida.

s: Which State is India's largest software exporter?
x: Karnataka accounts for over a third of India's software exports.

s: Which city is nicknamed "Cyberabad"?
x: Hyderabad is Cyberabad; Bengaluru is the Silicon Valley of India.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Visakhapatnam — Parawada Pharma City and Hindustan Shipyard
x: Dholera is associated with a semiconductor fabrication unit, not the Kia automobile manufacturing unit. Sri City is associated with Isuzu and Foxconn, Sri Sathya Sai with Kia, and Visakhapatnam with Parawada Pharma City and Hindustan Shipyard.

s: In which year was the India Semiconductor Mission launched?
x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in 2021.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The semiconductor fabrication unit is associated with Dholera. Micron’s ATMP unit is at Sanand, while Tata’s ₹27,000-crore semiconductor plant is at Jagiroad in Assam.

s: Where is Micron's ATMP semiconductor unit located?
x: Sanand hosts the Micron ATMP; Dholera is the fab and Jagiroad the Tata plant.

s: The electronics PLI grew out of which policy?
x: The electronics PLI grew out of the National Policy on Electronics 2019, giving 4–6% incentives.

s: Where is Tata's ₹27,000-crore semiconductor plant, announced in March 2024, located?
x: Tata's ₹27,000-crore plant is at Jagiroad in Assam; Dholera has the fab and Sanand the Micron ATMP unit.

s: What electronics production target has Andhra Pradesh set for 2024-29?
x: AP's electronics plan (2024-29) targets US$ 50 bn production and 5 lakh jobs.

s: Bulk Drug Parks are associated with which group of States?
o: Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh
Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Punjab
x: Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh are the States associated with Bulk Drug Parks.

s: India is called the 'Pharmacy of the World'. What are its ranks by production volume and export value respectively?
x: India is known as the “Pharmacy of the World”; it ranks third by pharmaceutical production volume and eleventh by export value.

s: Near which city is Parawada Pharma City located?
x: Parawada Pharma City is a pharmaceutical cluster at Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which city of India is the main hub for bulk drugs?
x: Hyderabad is the bulk drug hub; Ahmedabad-Vadodara and Parawada (Visakhapatnam) are other pharma hubs.

s: Which one of the following is an agro-based industry?
x: Cotton textiles are agro-based because cotton is an agricultural raw material. Cement, aluminium and iron and steel are mineral-based industries.

s: Dairy is an example of which type of industry?
x: Dairy is animal-based; sugar is agro-based, pulp and paper forest-based and coastal aquaculture processing marine-based.

s: Which of the following is a forest-based industry?
x: Lac is forest-based, like matchsticks, resin, bamboo products and rayon; petrochemicals and oil refining are fuel-based, leather animal-based.

s: Why do agro-based industrial units generally locate near the source of raw materials?
x: Agricultural raw materials may be perishable or lose weight in processing, so units locate near them.

s: Coastal aquaculture processing is classified as which type of industry?
x: Industries based on sea produce, such as seafood and coastal aquaculture processing, are marine-based.

s: Which is the largest forest-based industry?
x: Pulp and paper is the largest forest-based industry.

s: On which raw material is rayon, or artificial silk, based?
x: Rayon is made from wood pulp, so it is a forest-based industry.

s: Which of the following is NOT a mineral-based industry?
x: Plywood is made from timber, so it is forest-based; cement, copper smelting and aluminium use minerals.

s: In Andhra Pradesh's industrial map, leather and auto parts are associated with which district?
x: Leather and auto parts are associated with Nellore; Prakasam is associated with mineral-based industries.

s: What is India's per capita paper consumption?
x: India's per capita consumption is about 16 kg; 57 kg is the world figure.

s: Which industry is led by China, India and Indonesia?
x: Rayon is led by China, India and Indonesia; paper and pulp by China, USA, Japan, Germany, Finland, Sweden and Canada.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: China, USA, Japan, Germany, Finland, Sweden and Canada are leading countries or regions for Paper and Pulp.
Rayon or artificial silk is based on wood pulp.
China is the largest furniture importer.
China, USA, Germany, Italy, Vietnam and Indonesia are leading countries or regions for Furniture and Plywood.
x: Option C is incorrect: China is the largest furniture exporter, not importer. The paper, rayon and furniture producer lists are right.

s: Which of the following characterises the paper and pulp industry?
x: Paper and pulp mills need heavy machinery, chemicals and power, so the industry is capital-intensive; Finland, Sweden and Canada are leading exporters.

s: Which countries are the top exporters of paper?
x: Finland, Sweden and Canada are the top paper exporters; China, India and Indonesia lead in rayon.

s: Which country is the largest exporter of furniture?
x: China is the largest furniture exporter.

s: In paper making, recycled fibre makes up about what share of the raw material?
x: Recycled fibre is 71-75% of the raw material; wood pulp is about 21%.

s: Which country is now the top producer of wood pulp as per FAO 2025?
x: FAO 2025 data put the USA at the top in wood pulp production; Canada is the largest exporter of soft timber and wood pulp.

s: Which of the following is NOT a fuel-based industry?
x: Paper and pulp is forest-based; the other three are fuel-based.

s: Which of the following is a manpower-based industry?
x: Handloom is labour-intensive (manpower-based); the other three are fuel-based.

s: Thermal power accounts for about what share of industrial water use in India?
x: Thermal power is the largest industrial water user at about 88%; engineering uses about 5%.

s: In India, in which sector is the maximum amount of coal used?
x: Most of India's coal is burnt in thermal power stations to produce electricity.

s: Mallavalli in Andhra Pradesh is associated with which agro-based facility?
x: Mallavalli has a Mega Food Park (agro-based); steel is at Visakhapatnam and leather in Nellore.

s: Which districts of Andhra Pradesh are noted for mineral-based industries?
x: Prakasam and Kurnool are the State's mineral-based industry districts; Nellore is known for leather and auto parts.

s: Maruti Udyog was originally an example of which type of ownership?
o: Joint sector (Government of India and Suzuki)
x: Maruti Udyog was originally a joint-sector undertaking of the Government of India and Suzuki.

s: Which of the following pairs of ownership type and example is correctly matched?
x: Amul is a cooperative; BHEL is public sector, JSW private sector and APIIC joint ventures joint sector.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, to whom were Schedule B industries open?
x: Schedule B was open to both sectors; Schedule A (arms, atomic energy, iron and steel) was reserved for the public sector.

s: Which of the following pairs of industry and ownership sector is correctly matched?
x: NALCO is a public-sector unit. BHEL is public, JSW private and Maharashtra sugar mills cooperative.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, for which sector were Schedule A industries such as arms and atomic energy reserved?
x: Schedule A (arms, atomic energy, iron and steel) was for the public sector; Schedule B was open to both.

s: The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises was formed in 2007 by merging which two ministries?
o: Ministry of Rural Development and Ministry of Agriculture
Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industries
Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Small Scale Industries and Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries
x: The Ministry of MSME was formed in 2007 by merging the Ministry of Small Scale Industries with the Ministry of Agro and Rural Industries.

s: The 2020 definition of MSMEs introduced which major change?
o: Classification exclusively by number of workers
A composite criterion of investment and turnover, without distinguishing manufacturing from services
x: The 2020 definition uses a composite criterion of investment and turnover and removes the earlier distinction between manufacturing and service enterprises.

s: From 1 April 2025, what is the investment limit of a micro enterprise?
x: Micro: investment up to ₹2.5 crore and turnover up to ₹10 crore.

s: From 1 April 2025, what is the turnover ceiling of a medium enterprise?
x: Medium: investment up to ₹125 crore and turnover up to ₹500 crore; ₹100 crore is the small-enterprise turnover limit.

s: From 1 April 2025, what is the investment limit of a small enterprise?
x: A small enterprise may invest up to ₹25 crore with turnover up to ₹100 crore; ₹2.5 crore is the micro limit and ₹125 crore the medium limit.

s: In the use-based classification of industries, under which class do appliances fall?
x: Appliances are consumer durables; machinery is capital goods, chemicals intermediate goods and food consumer non-durables.

s: The term 'gold collar' is associated with which sector?
x: The quinary sector, involving top-level decision-making, is called the 'gold collar' sector.

s: Which one of the following is classified as a basic or primary good?
x: Steel, cement and coal are examples of basic or primary goods.

s: Which of the following is a sunset industry?
x: Legacy print and thermal coal equipment are sunset areas; green hydrogen, EVs, semiconductors and AI are sunrise areas.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Heavy industries are always labour-intensive, while light industries are always capital-intensive.
2. Heavy industries use bulky inputs and produce bulky outputs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Heavy industries have bulky inputs and outputs and are generally capital-intensive; light industries use lighter inputs and make consumer goods, so statement 1 is wrong.

s: How many use-based classes are employed in the Index of Industrial Production?
x: The IIP uses six use-based classes: primary, capital, intermediate, infrastructure/construction, consumer durables and consumer non-durables. There is no export goods class.

s: Diamond polishing and software are examples of which type of industry?
x: Footloose industries need skilled labour and internet, not a particular raw material.

s:
Consider the following statements about heavy and light industries:
1. Heavy industries are bulky and capital-intensive, such as HEC Ranchi.
2. Electronics assembly and garments are light industries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Heavy industries such as iron and steel and HEC Ranchi are bulky and capital-intensive; light industries such as electronics assembly and garments use lighter inputs.

s: Which of the following is NOT a use-based class of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
x: The IIP has six use-based classes: primary, capital, intermediate, infrastructure/construction, consumer durables and consumer non-durables. There is no export goods class.

s: Which industry carries the highest weight in the revised Index of Core Industries (base 2022-23)?
x: Electricity has the highest weight (about 31%); the revised index has base 2022-23 and nine industries with iron ore added.

s: The Perform, Achieve and Trade scheme is moving to the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme for how many sectors?
x: Nine sectors, including cement, fertilisers, paper, textiles, petrochemicals and refining.

s: How many industries make up the revised Index of Core Industries (base 2022-23)?
x: The revised index has nine industries after iron ore was added; electricity has the highest weight.

s: The Index of Eight Core Industries (ICI) and the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) were both rebased in July of which year?
x: Both the ICI and the IIP were rebased in 2026, with the new series released in July 2026.

s: In the Index of Core Industries rebased to 2022-23, which industry carries the highest weight?
x: Electricity has the heaviest weight (30.93), ahead of refinery products (22.57) and steel (17.58).

s: After rebasing to 2022-23, how many industries does the Index of Core Industries cover?
x: With iron ore added, the index now covers 9 industries, not 8.

s: Which industry was newly added to the Index of Core Industries in its 2022-23 base?
x: Iron ore is the newest member, taking the index from 8 to 9 industries.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the industries in the Index of Core Industries?
x: The nine core industries are electricity, refinery products, steel, crude oil, coal, iron ore, cement, natural gas and fertilizers; textiles is not one.

s: In the Index of Core Industries (base 2022-23), which industry has the second-highest weight after electricity?
x: Refinery products carry 22.57, next only to electricity (30.93); steel is third at 17.58.
